name: Wi-Fi access point
description: A 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g access point with a router behind it, as a home router is seen from a station across the room: it beacons its SSID every beacon interval, answers probe requests, authenticates (open system) and associates stations, runs WPA2-Personal's 4-way handshake and CCMP, leases them addresses by DHCP, answers ARP and pings for its own address, relays frames between its stations and keeps frames for dozing ones. It reaches the circuit only through the air; its signal reaches a board at the free-space path loss over their distance on the bench.

password.doc: The WPA2-Personal passphrase (8 to 63 characters); empty for an open network

channel.doc: The 2.4 GHz channel (1 to 13, 14 in Japan)

beacon_interval.doc: The time between beacons, in 1024 us time units

ip.doc: The router's address on its /24 network; stations lease .100 onwards by DHCP

bssid.doc: Its MAC address (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff); empty for a locally administered one from its name

outputs.name: mac
outputs.doc: Its MAC address, the network's BSSID

outputs.name: log
outputs.doc: What its stations did: authenticated, associated (with the AID), leased an address, disassociated, deauthenticated

functional.claims: Beacons (TSF timestamp, interval, ESS and privacy capabilities, SSID, rates, DS parameter set, TIM with the AIDs it keeps frames for, ERP, the WPA2-Personal RSN element with a password) every beacon interval at 1 Mbit/s, every one a DTIM; probe responses to wildcard and matching probe requests; open system authentication; association and reassociation with AIDs from 1; deauthentication and disassociation (IEEE 802.11-2020 9.3.3, 11.3); WPA2-Personal: the PSK from the passphrase and SSID, the 4-way handshake (the PTK from both nonces and addresses, the MICs, the GTK wrapped under the KEK in message 3, message 1 or 3 sent again after a second without an answer, four times), then CCMP on every data frame, pairwise to a station and group (key ID 1) to all, the PN checked against replay (12.7.6, 12.5.3); data frames with 802.2 LLC/SNAP to and from its stations (unicast at 54 Mbit/s, group at 1 Mbit/s); its stations' power management: frames kept for a dozing station, announced in the TIM, sent on a PS-Poll with More Data or when it wakes, group frames after the DTIM beacon (11.2.3); the router behind it: ARP for its address, ICMP echo, a DHCP server (RFC 2131, 2132: DISCOVER, OFFER, REQUEST, ACK, NAK, DECLINE, RELEASE; mask, router, DNS server, broadcast address, a day's lease) leasing .100 onwards; relaying frames between its stations. Frames carry their airtime and reach stations at the free-space path loss over the bench distance (engine/air.h). ESP-IDF's wifi/getting_started/station joins it, open or WPA2-PSK, and gets its address.
omissions: group key rekeying, PMKSA caching, WPA2-Enterprise, TKIP and protected management frames
the network beyond the router: DNS answers, TCP and UDP to the host
802.11n (HT capabilities and operation), WMM and QoS
more than 8 stations, more than 32 frames kept for dozing ones (the oldest is dropped)
the interframe timing of a real AP's firmware: responses follow a received frame after its ACK and DIFS

electrical.claims: As functional: it has no pins.

sources.title: IEEE Std 802.11-2020: frame formats (9.3.3), elements (9.4.2), authentication and association (11.3)
sources.notes: The beacon, probe response, authentication and association frames and their fields; the RSN element of WPA2-Personal (CCMP pairwise and group, PSK).
